label: <DEL> step (and new-token original steps) in sequences starting with g/u/p/i/2/3
explanation: Most activation mass (65%) is at the <DEL> step (7.4x lift), with the rest on original-phase steps t>=3 where the input is a first occurrence, especially k/v/a/w/n. Copy-phase steps (t>L) almost never fire (1% of mass). Whether it fires depends strongly on the first original token, the one about to be output: g (5.5x), u, p, i, 3, 2. The largest activations (near max) are <DEL> steps in short sequences starting with g or u. Even so, only about 27% of <DEL> steps whose first token is in that set actually fire. Adding conditions on which other tokens appeared earlier (e.g. absence of z/m/x/c/l/y) raised precision only slightly, so the unit looks like a distributed readout of sequence content rather than a clean single feature. Does not fire at t<2 or on repeated tokens.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the token being output, by phase (delimiter step: g, i, u, p; copy phase: g, u, 3, p; input phase: -) and the next token to output (most: u, g, p, 3, 2, i; least: a, w, x, m); timing cues that raise it most: t=4, t=3, t=5.
